claims.text: Increasing lattice distortion in high-entropy-alloy protective coatings improves wear resistance.
Increased lattice distortion enhances solid-solution strengthening.
Solid-solution strengthening restricts dislocation motion during wear.
Restricted dislocation motion reduces plastic deformation during wear.
Reduced dislocation mobility and plastic deformation lower abrasion wear rates.
The proposed test system consists of homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy-alloy coatings.
Substituting constituent elements with atoms of different radii can systematically modulate lattice distortion while retaining high-entropy-alloy criteria.
Atomic-size mismatch is a quantifiable measure of the degree of lattice distortion.
Coatings with greater lattice distortion will have lower wear rates than coatings with lower lattice distortion under otherwise identical test conditions.
Coatings with greater lattice distortion will have lower coefficients of friction than coatings with lower lattice distortion under otherwise identical test conditions.
Using elements with similar atomic radii produces a baseline coating with minimal lattice distortion.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold for single-phase high-entropy-alloy coatings under moderate wear conditions.
The proposed mechanism may cease to hold under extreme loads or temperatures that induce phase changes.
Prior evidence supports the direction of the proposed lattice-distortion effect on wear resistance.
